Hi there! Thanks for checking on this before launching — that's exactly the right instinct. Based on the license docs, here's how your setup looks:

**The short answer: as described, this likely falls outside the Community license.**

The key issue isn't that you're charging for n8n specifically — it's that you'd be **giving users access to the n8n instance itself so they can build their own workflows**. The license explicitly prohibits:

- "Host n8n as a service and allow your clients to build workflows" [3]
- "Allow external end users to build or configure their own workflows through your product, whether via a custom UI, our API, MCP, or an AI agent acting on the user's behalf." [3]

Sending an invitation link so subscribers can log in and build workflows with your API hits this directly.

**What *would* be allowed** is using n8n purely behind the scenes: "Use n8n behind the scenes in your own product, where users can use and trigger the automations you built, and even connect their own accounts to them" [5] — as long as "only your backend communicates with n8n, and end users do not access n8n UI or configure n8n workflows" [3]. Similarly, you can build automations *for* clients on your instance "as long as your clients do not have the possibility to create or edit them" [5].

**One more wrinkle:** even framing it as a "free bonus" doesn't sidestep things, since the Sustainable Use License only lets you distribute the software "free of charge for non-commercial purposes" [4] — and here it's bundled with a paid subscription.

**What to do next:** Since your use case isn't clearly covered, the docs recommend reaching out directly. For licensing questions, contact **license@n8n.io**, and to discuss a commercial agreement, contact **sales@n8n.io** [3]. A separate commercial agreement is the path if you want to offer n8n access to your subscribers [2].

Good luck with the project — and definitely worth a quick email to the licensing team to confirm your final architecture!

Happy to help with this one! One important caveat first: the docs I have here don't include the Airtable node reference, so I can't cite exact Airtable field names — but the pattern you're describing maps cleanly onto documented n8n features, and I can point you to the right pieces.

## 1. Get structured JSON out of the chat message

Use an **AI Agent** node and turn on **Require Specific Output Format**. The agent then returns an object on the `structuredOutput` field matching the schema you define [1]. You can either paste a JSON example (every property becomes required) or write a JSON Schema yourself [1].

⚠️ Note the caveat: structured output is enforced by the model provider, so support varies. Mark every property as required for the most reliable results — some providers reject optional fields or advanced keywords [1]. Practically, that means you'd make `age`, `gender`, `weight` all required but allow `null` values, then have the agent return `null` for anything not mentioned. That gives you your "only mentioned fields update" signal.

## 2. Steer the extraction behavior with a System Message

The Conversational AI Agent node has a **System Message** option — a message sent to the agent before the conversation starts, which you can use to guide the agent's decision-making [3]. This is the right place for instructions like "extract only the fields the customer explicitly stated; return null for all others; never guess."

## 3. Update only the non-null fields

The Microsoft Dataverse node docs describe exactly the pattern you need: for an **Update**, you send *only the fields you want to change*, e.g. `{"telephone1": "555-0100"}` updates just the phone number without replacing the other fields [2]. Airtable's update operation works the same way conceptually — so:

1. Add a **Code node** (or Filter/If) after the agent to strip out `null` keys, leaving only the fields the customer actually mentioned.
2. Pass that object to your Airtable **Update** operation, targeting the existing record by its record ID.
3. Store that record ID (e.g. in the conversation memory or keyed by chat/session ID) so each subsequent turn updates the *same* row and accumulates data.

That combination gives you the incremental profile-building behavior you want without overwriting previously collected values.

## Caveat

I can't confirm the exact Airtable node input options from the excerpts I was given. For the Airtable specifics (how to pass a fields object, record ID handling), check https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.airtable/ or ask in the n8n community forum — someone there has almost certainly built this exact chat-to-profile pattern.

The empty result is almost certainly caused by the download step, not the extraction step. 👍

**What's happening**

In your **Download file** node, the `googleFileConversion` option is empty (`conversion: {}`) — you never told Google Drive what format to export the Google Doc as. Google Docs aren't stored as regular files, so they have to be converted on download. With no export format selected, the binary that comes through is empty/unusable, so **Extract from File** has nothing to read.

**The fix**

1. Open your **Download file** node.
2. Under **Options → Google File Conversion**, expand **Google Docs** and select **HTML**.

Per the node docs, the Google Docs export options are **HTML**, **MS Word Document**, **Open Office Document**, **PDF**, **Rich Text (rtf)**, or **Text (txt)** — pick one of those (HTML for your case) [5].
3. Keep **Put Output File in Field** as `data` (or whatever field your Extract node expects).
4. Re-run. The **Extract from File** node with the **Extract From HTML** operation should now find content [4].

**Alternative for getting raw HTML**

If you don't need a specific export conversion and just want the HTML markup as a field, you can also use the **HTML** node's **Extract HTML Content** operation, which takes an HTML source (JSON or a binary `.html` file) and extracts content from it [6].

One small heads-up: if you later generate HTML with the HTML node, be careful with un-trusted inputs due to XSS risk [6] — not an issue for what you're doing now.

Give the conversion setting a try and see if data flows through — that should sort it out!

Hey! Good question — and the short version is: you shouldn't need to re-pull those 1000+ tickets at all. Two angles worth considering:

**1. Skip the loop entirely**

By default, n8n nodes are built to process a whole list of input items automatically — each node runs once per item, so you often don't need the Loop Over Items node at all [2][3]. That means you can:

- Fetch the Linear tickets **once** (as a single list).
- Fetch the PRs **once** (as a single list).
- Then do the enrichment in a **Code node set to "Run Once for All Items"**, matching each PR's ticket number against the ticket list and attaching the ticket data. Hi there! Thanks for the kind words — and I completely understand where you're coming from. Unfortunately, none of the documentation I have access to covers interface localization or multilingual support (including Chinese Simplified), so I can't confirm whether it's planned or share a timeline. I don't want to guess on your behalf.

Here's what I'd suggest:

- **Ask in the n8n community forum** — it's the best place for questions of all kinds, and both the n8n team and community members respond there. Someone from the team may be able to speak to roadmap plans, and you may find other users interested in translation work [3].
- **Check the contribution guide** — if you're interested in helping with translations, the docs include a "Get help with n8n" / contributing section, which is a good starting point for reaching the right people [3].
- **Email support** — if you're on an Enterprise plan, you can use email support (help@n8n.io) for account and roadmap questions; other plans can use it for admin and billing topics [3].

One thing that might help in the meantime: **n8n Assistant** lets you describe what you want to automate in plain natural language, and it plans, builds, tests, and troubleshoots the workflow for you in a chat — which could lower the barrier when explaining things to teammates [1][5]. It's still in Preview, so review anything it generates before production use [1].

Sorry I can't give you a definitive answer on Chinese support — the forum is your best bet for an official response. 🙂
